title: Context pin
description: Marks a load-bearing object (a pending hotpath receipt, an open negative_result, a runtime pin) as non-compressible by a context summarizer. Distinct from handoff.json, which covers an explicit agent-to-agent transfer boundary -- a pin exists because the SAME agent's own harness can silently summarize or truncate mid-task with no detectable edge at all. Not an evidence-gated pattern: no AF-#### backs this, and none should be minted for it without a real, dated, sourced incident of pinned state actually being dropped in a specific product. The mechanism is well-discussed in agent-scaffolding literature (context compaction silently dropping a pending tool result or task dependency) but every source found is general technical analysis, not a specific documented event.
